examples.ko: 설거지는 개수대에서 하고 그릇은 옆에 놓아요.
examples.en: I wash the dishes in the sink and put the bowls next to it.

examples.ko: 개수대가 막혀서 물이 잘 안 내려가요.
examples.en: The sink is clogged, so the water doesn't drain well.
I put the dish soap and scrubber next to the sink.

examples.ko: 개수대 안에 그릇이 가득 쌓여 있어요.
examples.en: The sink is full of piled-up dishes.

examples.ko: 새 집은 개수대가 넓어서 설거지하기 편해요.
examples.en: The new house has a wide sink, so washing dishes is easy.
I wipe the sink clean every morning.

explain: '싱크대'는 개수대와 조리대가 붙은 주방 가구 전체를 말하고, '개수대'는 그중 물을 쓰고 설거지하는 움푹 들어간 부분만 가리켜요. 일상에서는 '싱크대'라고 하는 경우가 많고, '개수대'는 설명서나 공공시설 안내에서 더 잘 보여요.

phrases.en: I left the dishes soaking in the sink.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '개수대'보다 '싱크대'를 훨씬 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily speech 싱크대 is used far more often than 개수대.

phrases.en: I wash vegetables in the sink.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '에서'를 붙여 물을 쓰는 일을 하는 장소를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With the particle 에서 to name the place where you use water.

phrases.en: I cleaned the sink thoroughly on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주방 청소 이야기에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing when talking about kitchen cleaning.

explain_en: '싱크대' is the whole kitchen unit with the basin and counter, while '개수대' is just the recessed part where you use water and wash dishes. In daily talk people often say '싱크대', and '개수대' shows up more in manuals and public-facility notices.

examples.en: I locked the door by hooking the latch.

examples.ko: 걸쇠가 고장 나서 문이 저절로 열려요.
examples.en: The latch is broken, so the door opens by itself.
I need to install a new window latch.
I undid the latch and carefully opened the door.
The clasp on my necklace came off, and I lost it.
The clasp on my bag won't lock.

explain: 문이나 창문을 걸어 잠그는 쇠붙이를 말해요. 가로로 지르는 긴 막대인 '빗장'과는 달리 갈고리처럼 걸리는 부분이에요. 목걸이나 가방의 잠금 장치도 '걸쇠'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I latch the door when I sleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문을 잠글 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for latching a door shut.

phrases.en: I undid the latch and opened the door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잠근 걸쇠를 열 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for releasing a latch that was fastened.

phrases.en: The necklace clasp is small, so it's hard to fasten.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문뿐 아니라 목걸이나 가방의 잠금 장치도 '걸쇠'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Besides doors, the clasp on a necklace or bag is also called '걸쇠'.

explain_en: It is the metal piece that hooks a door or window shut. Unlike a '빗장', which is a long bar across a door, it is a hook-like catch. The fastening on a necklace or bag can also be called '걸쇠'.

examples.ko: 파운데이션을 덧발랐더니 얼굴이 너무 하얘 보여요.
examples.en: I put on more foundation and now my face looks too white.

examples.ko: 벽에 페인트를 한 번 더 덧발랐어요.
examples.en: I put another coat of paint on the wall.

examples.ko: 선크림은 두 시간마다 덧바르는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It is good to reapply sunscreen every two hours.
When I reapply lip balm, my lips feel moist.

examples.ko: 약을 덧바르지 말고 얇게 한 번만 바르세요.
examples.en: Don't layer on the ointment; apply it thinly just once.

examples.ko: 얼룩이 보여서 그 위에 덧발라 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a stain, so I tried covering it with another layer.

explain: '르' 불규칙이라 '덧발라요, 덧발랐어요'가 돼요. 이미 바른 곳에 한 번 더 바를 때 쓰고, 페인트처럼 색을 입히는 경우에는 '덧칠하다'도 많이 말해요. 말을 더 보탤 때는 '덧붙이다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 낮에 선크림을 한 번 더 덧발라요.
phrases.en: I reapply sunscreen once more during the day.
phrases.nuance_ko: '르' 불규칙 해요체를 알아 두면 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Worth knowing the irregular polite form of this verb.

phrases.example: 크림은 너무 많이 덧바르지 않는 게 좋아요.
phrases.en: It's better not to reapply the cream too much.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하지 말라고 조언할 때 쓰는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form used when giving advice not to do it.

phrases.en: The wall was stained, so I painted over it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색을 칠하는 경우에는 이 말도 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This word is also very common when applying color.

explain_en: It is a '르' irregular verb, so it becomes '덧발라요' and '덧발랐어요'. It is used for applying another layer on a spot already covered, and for paint or color '덧칠하다' is also common. To add more words to what you said, use '덧붙이다'.

examples.ko: 가방 안에서 비닐봉지가 바스락 소리를 내요.
examples.en: A plastic bag rustles inside my bag.

examples.ko: 낙엽을 밟을 때마다 바스락 소리가 나요.
examples.en: Every time I step on fallen leaves, there's a crunchy rustle.

examples.ko: 밤에 방에서 바스락 소리가 나서 깼어요.
examples.en: A rustling sound in my room at night woke me up.
The child rustled open the snack bag.
I can hear the rustle of paper being folded.

examples.ko: 이불 속에서 바스락 움직이는 소리가 났어요.
examples.en: There was a rustling sound of someone moving under the blanket.

explain: 마른 잎, 종이, 비닐 같은 것이 스치거나 움직일 때 나는 가벼운 소리예요. '바스락 소리가 나다'처럼 자주 쓰고, 더 크고 둔한 느낌의 말은 '부스럭'이에요.

phrases.en: I heard a rustling sound in the room at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '바스락'과 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing with 바스락.

phrases.en: The snack bag keeps rustling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 여러 번 이어질 때 반복해서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The repeated form for a sound that continues.

phrases.en: There's a rustling sound from the next room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '바스락'보다 더 크고 둔한 소리예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A louder, duller sound than 바스락.

explain_en: It is the light sound of dry leaves, paper or plastic brushing or moving. You often hear '바스락 소리가 나다'. The bigger, duller version is '부스럭'.

examples.en: I wiped the floor and now it shines.

examples.ko: 아이가 반들반들 닳은 돌을 주워 왔어요.
examples.en: The child picked up a smooth, worn stone.
I polished my shoes until they gleamed.
The wooden handle, used for a long time, is smooth and shiny.
I polished the apple until it was shiny and then ate it.

examples.ko: 새로 산 차가 햇빛에 반들반들 빛나요.
examples.en: The newly bought car gleams in the sunlight.

explain: 표면이 매끄럽고 윤이 날 때 써요. '번들번들'은 기름기가 있어 번지르르한 느낌이 들 때가 있고, '반들반들'은 깨끗하고 매끈한 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: My new shoes are glossy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-하다'를 붙여 표면 상태를 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -하다 describes the state of a surface.

phrases.en: I slipped on the shiny floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to modify a noun that follows.

phrases.en: I wiped the window until it shone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 닦아서 윤이 나게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when wiping something until it shines.

explain_en: Used when a surface is smooth and shiny. '번들번들' can feel greasy or slick, while '반들반들' feels clean and sleek.

examples.ko: 낡은 문이 삐걱 소리를 내며 열렸어요.
examples.en: The old door opened with a creak.

examples.ko: 계단을 오를 때마다 삐걱 소리가 나요.
examples.en: The stairs creak every time I go up.
The bed creaked, so I slept badly at night.

examples.ko: 새 시스템을 도입한 뒤 부서 간 협업이 삐걱거리기 시작했어요.
examples.en: After the new system was introduced, collaboration between departments started to stumble.

examples.ko: 두 사람 사이가 요즘 삐걱거리는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems things between those two have been rocky lately.
The wooden floor kept creaking, so I walked very carefully.

explain: 나무나 쇠가 서로 쓸릴 때 나는 소리를 흉내 낸 말이에요. 문, 의자, 계단, 마루에 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '삐걱거리다' 꼴로 훨씬 자주 말해요. 비유로 사이가 안 좋거나 일이 순조롭지 않을 때도 써요.

phrases.en: The team atmosphere has been rocky lately, and I'm worried.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 사이나 일이 매끄럽게 돌아가지 않고 불안하게 흔들리는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a relationship or process that is not running smoothly and feels shaky.
phrases.en_equiv: be on shaky ground; hit a rough patch

explain_en: It imitates the sound of wood or metal rubbing together, used for doors, chairs, stairs and floors. In daily talk the form '삐걱거리다' is much more common. It is also used figuratively when a relationship or a task is not going smoothly.

examples.en: The curtain slid open softly.
The snake slithered quietly into the grass.
The hair tie slipped loose.
I'm sleepy, and my eyelids are drooping.
The door closed softly.

examples.ko: 안심이 되자 몸에서 힘이 스르륵 빠졌어요.
examples.en: When I felt relieved, the strength drained from my body.

explain: '스르르'와 거의 같지만 무언가 살짝 스치듯 미끄러지는 소리와 느낌이 조금 더 들어 있어요. 문, 커튼, 매듭이 소리 없이 움직일 때나 힘이 빠질 때 써요.

phrases.en: The sled slid smoothly over the snow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리 없이 부드럽게 미끄러지는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has a feeling of sliding smoothly and quietly.

phrases.en: My shoelace came undone with a soft slip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 매듭이나 끈이 쉽게 풀리는 모습에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits knots or strings coming loose easily.

phrases.en: The elevator door closed softly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문이 조용하고 부드럽게 움직일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a door moves quietly and smoothly.

explain_en: It is almost the same as '스르르' but carries a bit more of the sound and feel of something sliding past lightly. It is used for doors, curtains and knots moving quietly, or for strength draining away.

examples.en: A bell jingles on the cat's neck.

examples.ko: 가방에 단 열쇠고리가 잘랑잘랑 소리를 내요.
examples.en: The keychain on my bag makes a jingling sound.
I heard a jingling sound and turned around.
The wind chime sways and jingles in the wind.

examples.ko: 아이가 걸을 때마다 신발의 방울이 잘랑잘랑 울렸어요.
examples.en: Every time the child walked, the bell on the shoe jingled.

examples.ko: 주머니 속 동전이 잘랑잘랑 소리를 냈어요.
examples.en: The coins in my pocket made a jingling sound.

explain: 작은 방울이나 쇠붙이가 가볍게 흔들리며 나는 소리를 흉내 낸 말이에요. 같은 소리를 더 또렷하고 센 느낌으로 말할 때는 '짤랑짤랑'을 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.example: 걸을 때마다 가방에서 잘랑잘랑 소리가 나요.
phrases.en: My bag jingles every time I walk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 방울이나 쇠붙이가 흔들리며 소리를 낼 때 가장 흔하게 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for the sound of a small bell or metal piece shaking.

phrases.en: The keychain jingles and sways on my bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리와 함께 가볍게 움직이는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes light movement together with a jingling sound.

phrases.en: The coins jingle in my pocket.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잘랑잘랑'에서 나온 동사로, 같은 소리가 계속 날 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A verb from 잘랑잘랑, used when the same sound keeps going.

explain_en: It imitates the light sound of small bells or bits of metal shaking. '짤랑짤랑' is sometimes used for the same sound with a sharper, stronger feel.

examples.en: I tidied my eyebrows with tweezers while looking in the mirror.
A thorn got stuck in my hand, so I looked for tweezers.
You need tweezers to pull out a thorn.
I took cram tutoring before the exam.
The tweezers are in the medicine box.

examples.ko: 족집게에 끼운 털이 잘 안 빠져요.
examples.en: The hair caught in the tweezers will not come out easily.

explain: 털이나 가시처럼 작은 것을 집어 뽑는 도구예요. '핀셋'도 비슷한 도구인데 '핀셋'은 실험, 의료, 공예 같은 정밀한 작업에서 더 자주 떠올라요. 도구 이름에서 나온 비유로 정확히 집어내는 사람이나 선생님을 말하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 그 선생님은 시험에 나올 문제를 족집게처럼 맞히세요.
phrases.en: That teacher predicts the exam questions with uncanny accuracy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 가시를 쏙 뽑는 도구처럼, 딱 집어서 정확히 알아맞힌다는 뜻이에요. 정확한 예측에 감탄할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like a tool that plucks out a tiny thorn, it means picking out exactly the right thing. Used to admire very accurate guesses or predictions.

phrases.en: I took cram tutoring that targets likely questions before the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험에 나올 만한 내용만 콕 집어 가르쳐 주는 과외나 강의예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Tutoring or a class that picks out only what is likely to appear on the exam.

explain_en: It is a tool for gripping and pulling small things like hairs or thorns. '핀셋' is a similar tool, but it brings to mind precision work such as experiments, medicine or crafts. By extension, it is also used figuratively for people or teachers who pick out the right thing exactly.

examples.en: It's vacation, so the classroom is totally empty.
It's the end of the month, so my wallet is totally empty.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에는 식당이 텅텅 비어요.
examples.en: On rainy days, the restaurant is totally empty.

examples.ko: 냉장고가 텅텅 비어서 장을 봐야 해요.
examples.en: The fridge is completely empty, so I have to go grocery shopping.
I was surprised that the parking lot was totally empty.
There were no customers, so the shop was totally empty.

explain: 거의 항상 '비다'와 함께 써서 '아무것도 없이 완전히 비어 있다'는 느낌을 줘요. '텅 비다'처럼 '텅'만 쓸 때보다 비어 있는 정도를 더 강조해요. 사람이 없는 장소와 돈이 없는 지갑에 모두 써요.

phrases.en: The fridge is totally empty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 비어 버린 상태를 말하는 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past form describing something that has become empty.

phrases.example: 집에 가니까 방이 텅 비어 있었어요.
phrases.en: When I got home, the room was completely empty.
phrases.nuance_ko: '텅텅'보다 짧고 조금 덜 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shorter and a bit less emphatic than '텅텅'.

phrases.example: 텅텅 빈 가게 앞에서 한참 서 있었어요.
phrases.en: I stood for a while in front of the empty shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사를 붙여 꾸밀 때 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used to modify a noun that follows.

explain_en: It almost always goes with '비다' and gives the feeling of being completely empty. It stresses the emptiness more than '텅' alone, as in '텅 비다'. It is used both for places with no people and for wallets with no money.
